 J U D G M E N T The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Vijayanagar Sub-Division, Bangalore City, has submitted charge sheet against the accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offence punishable U/s.498A and 304-B r/w.sec.34 of IPC and Section.3 and 4 of D.P.Act in Crime No.06/2023 of Govindarajanagar P.S.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage between the deceased Ramya and accused No.1 performed on 12.06.2022 according to the customs prevailed in their community at Smt.Rudramma Rudregowda Kalyana Mantapa situated at Kamakshipalya,
Bengaluru.
At the time of marriage, on demand, the accused persons received cash and gold ornaments.

After marriage without any reasons, the accused No.1 in intoxication condition harassed the deceased physically and mentally by abusing in filthy language by demanding the deceased to bring additional dowry of Rs.5 lakhs.

Because of continuous physical and mental harassment, the deceased on 10.01.2023 between 6.00 p.m. to 10.15 p.m committed suicide by hanging with the help of veil in the house bearing No.68, situated at Ist floor within the limits of Govindarajanagar police station and thereby the accused persons have committed the offences as alleged against them.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused persons.

The same was numbered as SC No.1279/2023.
4.
The prosecution has examined nineteen witnesses as PW.1 to PW.19 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P29 and MOs.1 to 10.
On consent of accused counsel, Post Mortem report has been marked at Ex.P.12.
As such the learned PP has gave up the witness CW.24.
This court has issued summons, warrant and proclamation against C.Ws.10, 11, 18 to 20.
Inspite of sufficient time granted, the concerned police failed to execute the same and keep present of C.Ws.10, 11, 18 to 20 before the court.
As such the prayer of the learned public prosecutor was rejected and the witnesses C.Ws.10, 11, 18 to 20 were dropped.
However the liberty has given to the prosecution for examination of C.Ws.10, 11, 18 to 20, if the concerned police keep present the said witnesses before the court before conclusion of the trial.

2 5.
The date of marriage of the deceased and accused No.1 in the charge is wrongly typed as 12.02.2022 instead of 12.06.2022.
Hence charge is modified and read over to the accused persons.
The accused persons have pleaded not guilty.
After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statements of accused persons, as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused persons have denied incriminating evidence present against them and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused persons have complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bonds and surety bonds.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 on 12.06.2022 got married the deceased Smt.Ramya according to the customs prevailed in their community at Smt.Rudramma Rudregowda Kalyana Mantapa situated the Kamakshipalya,
Bengaluru and at the time of marriage, on demand received cash and gold ornaments, later the accused started to harass the deceased by demanding additional dowry of Rs.5 lakhs and thereby the accused has committed the offence punishable under Sec.3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act?
2. Whether the prosecution proves that the marriage of accused No.1 with the deceased-Smt.Ramya, was solemnized on 12.06.2022 and at the time of marriage on demand accused persons received cash and gold ornaments and after the marriage deceased started to reside along with accused in rented house house bearing No.68,
situated at Ist floor within the limits of Govindarajanagar police station, the accused being the husband of deceased- Smt. Ramya subjected her to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry and thereby accused persons have committed offence punishable U/s.498A r/w. 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 ?
3. Whether the prosecution proves that the marriage of accused No.1 with the deceased-Smt.Ramya,
was solemnized on 12.06.2022, and at the time of marriage on demand accused persons received cash and gold ornaments and after the marriage deceased started to reside along with accused in rented house at house bearing No.68, situated at Ist floor within the limits of Govindarajanagar police station, accused being the husband of deceased- Smt. Ramya in intoxication condition subjected her to physical and mental cruelty in demanding additional dowry from her parents house, accused continued to harass the deceased in demanding additional dowry, and such cruelty and harassment did drive the said deceased-Smt.Ramya to commit suicide within seven years of marriage by hanging herself on 10.01.2023 in between 6.00 p.m. to 10.15 p.m at her matrimonial house and accused being her husband subjected her to cruelty and harassment in connection with the demand for additional dowry and thereby accused persons have committed offence of dowry death punishable U/s.304B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code,1860?

8. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9.
Points Nos.1 to 3: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.
The prosecution has examined prime witnesses cited in the charge sheet to establish the guilt against the accused persons.

On perusal of the prosecution papers and evidence of the parents,
brother, grandfather, sister and brother-in- law of the deceased Ramya clearly enumerates that the marriage of deceased Ramya and accused No.1 was performed on 12.06.2022.
The prosecution required to prove that at the time of marriage, the accused persons received dowry on demand from the parents of the deceased.
After the marriage, the accused No.1 used to quarrel with the deceased for silly reasons.
In fact the deceased was working in D-Mart and accused No.1 also working in a private company.

Even then, the accused No.1 alongwith other accused persons started to harass the deceased physically and mentally to bring additional dowry of Rs.5 lakhs to get mortgage the house for their livelihood as the accused No.1 not able to bear his monthly rent.

Due to the continuous physical and mental torture by the accused persons, the deceased become anguish and on 10.01.2023 between 6.00 p.m to 10.15 p.m committed suicide with the help of veil by hanging herself in her matrimonial house.
10.
To prove the said allegations, the parents of the deceased by name Mahadev, Radha examined as P.W.1 and P.W.5.
The parents of the deceased in their evidence never deposed demand of dowry by the accused persons prior to marriage or after marriage.
Even though deposed about the committing of suicide by the deceased, but they did not stated any reasons for committing of suicide by the deceased.
According to the complainant ie. father of the deceased Mahadev, somebody obtained his signatures on the complaint when he was in the shock due to the death of his daughter.
According to him, he has signed the Mahazar in police station.

The prosecution has got marked complaint, spot Mahazar at Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, photos taken at the time of conducting of Mahazar at Ex.P.3,
marriage invitation, photos and invoice at Ex.P.4 to Ex.P.6 and also got marked his signature present on the seizure Mahazar at Ex.P.7.
The complainant never deposed anything related with regard to the recitals of the complaint Ex.P.1, spot Mahazar Ex.P.2 and seizure Mahazar Ex.P.7.
According to him, the police have obtained his signatures on both Mahazar in the police station and nothing has been seized in his presence.
Even the mother of the deceased P.W.5 failed to narrate exact cause for committing of suicide by the deceased daughter.

Such being the case, the prosecution also examined the brother of the deceased P.W.6 Nithyananda, grandfather of the deceased P.W.11 Govindarajanagar P.S vs A1 Kiran on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192335769/
4 Puttaraju, sister of the deceased P.W.13 Soumya and brother-in-law of the deceased P.W.12 Rangaswamy as P.W.6, PW.11, P.W.12 and P.W.13.
All the said witnesses P.W.6, PW.11, P.W.12 and P.W.13 by name Nithyananda, Puttaraju, Soumya and Rangaswamy respectively never supported the prosecution story by becoming hostile.

Nevertheless the said witnesses have categorically stated about the marriage between the deceased Ramya and accused No.1, but not at all deposed anything related to the dowry harassment and due to the continuous dowry harassment by the accused persons, the deceased suffered and committed suicide.

As such the learned PP has treated the said witnesses P.W.1, P.W.5, P.W.6, PW.11, P.W.12 and P.W.13 as hostile with the permission of the court, perhaps not able to bring out any worthful evidence in support of the prosecution story.
Hence, the statements of the said witnesses P.W.5, P.W.6, PW.11, P.W.12 and P.W.13 have been marked at Ex.P.9, Ex.P.10, Ex.P.13, Ex.P.14, Ex.P.15 respectively.
So, it is very clear that the evidence of the family members of the deceased not at all helpful for the prosecution to prove the allegations made against the accused persons.
11. It is necessary to note that the panchas PW.2 Prasad and PW.3 Chandrashekar have failed to give evidence according to the recitals of the said spot Mahazar marked at Ex.P.2.
Even though they identified their presence in their photographs marked at Ex.P.3 document at the time of conducting of Mahazar, but their evidence not supports the prosecution story.
The evidence given by both PW.2 and P.W.3 not discloses seizure of veil at the time of conducting Mahazar as per Ex.P.2 by the Investigation Officer.
As such the learned PP has treated both P.W.2 and P.W.3 as hostile, but in the cross-examination not able to get any useful evidence to prove the said recitals of the Mahazar Ex.P.2.
Hence the evidence of both spot panchas PW.2 and P.W.3 not at all helpful for the prosecution to prove the Mahazar.

In fact the panchas being signatories to the seizure Mahazar marked at Ex.P.7 by name Maruthi and Chandan.S.Gowda also examined as P.W.10 and 14 respectively, also not supported the prosecution case by deposing that the police have obtained their signatures in Ex.P.7.
But they does not know the contents of Ex.P.7 and nothing has been seized in their presence.

Hence the evidence of both seizure panchas also not helpful for the prosecution to prove the said recitals of the Mahazar Ex.P.7.
12.
It is obvious to note that the prosecution examined Manjula, Siddegowda and Kantamma in support of the inquest Mahazar.
The said witness P.W.4 Manjula, P.W.7 Siddegowda and P.W.9 Kantamma deposed about the conducting of inquest Mahazar as per Ex.P.8.
Perhaps in the cross-examination the said witnesses straight away admitted that they does not know the contents of inquest Mahazar Ex.P.8.
It appears the Tahasildar and police have just obtained the signatures on Ex.P.8.
The witness P.W.9 Kantamma has completely turned hostile by deposing not conducting inquest Mahazar in her presence and she has not acquainted anything about the contents of Ex.P.8.

Though the learned PP has cross-examined P.W.9 Kantamma not able to get any useful evidence to prove the contents of the inquest Mahazar Ex.P.8.
13. It is necessary to note that the prosecution examined photographer by name Akhilash as P.W.8.
The said witness P.W.8 has carried out videograph and taken photos at the time of marriage of the deceased and accused No.1.
For which, the Investigation Officer has collected the certificate 65B as required under the Evidence Act marked at Ex.P.11.
The evidence given by the said witness has completely denied by the accused counsel.

As already discussed above, there is no dispute so far as Govindarajanagar P.S vs A1 Kiran on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192335769/
5 marriage of the deceased and accused No.1 is concerned.

The another witness Ramesh examined as P.W.15 has deposed that his elder aunt by name Hemavathi being the owner of the house has given one of the house on rental basis to the deceased and accused No.1 and collected the rental agreement.
After the death of Hemavathi, he has become the owner of the said house.
The prosecution has got marked rental agreement at Ex.P.16, perhaps he is not aware anything about the reasons for committing of suicide by the deceased.
According to him, he has not given statement before the police at any time.
As such the learned PP has cross-examined the said witness P.W.15 not able to bring out any useful evidence in support of the prosecution story.

14. It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.16 PC.No.20265 has given specific evidence that on 10.01.2023 at 11.30 p.m, when the ASI Lakshmi Kanthar was in SHO told him that the deceased has committed suicide and C.W.32 is present and told him to to go the place of incident situated at No.68, Pattegara Palya, when he went there at 11.40 p.m he found C.W.32, police staffs and neighbourers were present at the place of suicide and with the request of C.W.32 and deceased relatives, he break opened the door forcibly and found deceased has committed suicide and died,
later he sent the dead body of the deceased to Victoria hospital through Venkatesh police staff, later he went to do his work, he has given statement before C.W.33 with regard to the incident.

15. Further it is obvious to note that the witness P.W.17 PSI of Nandini Layout has given specific evidence that on 11.01.2023 issued instructions to police staff to secure the accused persons produced before him.
On 12.01.2023 at 5.00 p.m at Magadi road, Tolgate, secured accused No.1 Kiran at 5.30 p.m. and produced him before C.W.33.
Accordingly submitted the report and his signature.

The said report is marked at Ex.P.18.
16.

It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.18 Shivaprasad Dy.S.P Lokayuktha has given specific evidence that on 11.01.2023 when he was in the police station, C.W.1 came to police station and lodged complaint.

On the basis of the complaint, he has registered FIR vide Cr.No.06/2023 and sent the FIR to the court and his superior officers and he sent C.W.31 to look after the dead body at the place of incident.

On the next day at 9.00 a.m he secured the panchas C.W.2 and C.W.3 and issued notice and conducted spot Mahazar and seized the broken door lock piece and took signatures of C.W.1 and panchas and took photos as per Ex.P.2, Ex.P.3 and prepared sketch as per Ex.P.20.
He identified the door lock marked at M.O.1 and brought the seized M.O.1 into P.F. and submitted to the court.
Later he gave letter to C.W.23 to conduct post mortem and the said letter is marked at Ex.P.21.
After conducting post mortem handed over the dead body of the deceased to its relatives and collected endorsement.

Later handed over further investigation to C.W.33.
17.

It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.19 Ravi.P ACP has given specific evidence that on 12.01.2023 he received further investigation from P.W.18 and at 5.30 p.m the C.W.17 and police staffs of Govindarajnagar have traced and brought the accused No.1 before him and gave report as per Ex.P.18.

He has arrested the accused No.1 and recorded voluntary statement and seized gold chain and ring in the presence of panchas C.W.10 and C.W.11 and accordingly conducted panchanama as per Ex.P.25 and got marked the said material objects at M.O.2 and M.O.3, later he recorded statements of C.W.10 and 11.

On 13.01.2023 he sent the accused No.1 for medical examination and produced before the court alongwith remand application and on the same day Govindarajanagar P.S vs A1 Kiran on 20 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192335769/
6 C.W.1 came to the police station and produced the mobiles of deceased and accused No.1 in the presence of panchas C.W.12 and C.W.13.

C.W.16, on 15.01.2023 he received the P.M.Report as per Ex.P.12 and clothes and viscera of the deceased and brought into P.F.No.10/2023.
On 21.01.2023 he sent the clothes and viscera to FSL through C.W.27 and collected endorsement as per Ex.P.28.
The clothes of the deceased marked at M.O.6 to M.O.10, later he sent the requisition to the concerned company to give CDR.
On 23.01.2023 issued notice to the Manager of Kalyana Mantapa to give details of the marriage of accused No.1 and deceased.

On 24.01.2023 he received the documents from the Manager of Kalyana Mantapa, which are marked at Ex.P.29, on 25.01.2023, he recorded statement of C.W.18, on 27.01.2023 he recorded statements of C.W.19 and C.W.20.
On 16.02.2023 he recorded statement of C.W.21 and collected the rent agreement as per Ex.P.16 of the house, in which deceased and accused No.1 were residing.
On 17.03.2023 he recorded statements of C.W.24 and 25.
On 30.03.2023, he has completed the investigation and submitted charge sheet.
The evidence given by the police officials has completely denied by the accused counsel.
It is very clear from the above discussions that none of the independent witnesses have supported the case of the prosecution.
The evidence given by independent witnesses completely contrary to the evidence given by IOs. i.e. Police Officers.

So, it is very clear that the prosecution has completely failed to prove the allegations made against the accused persons to believe due to the continuous physical and mental harassment for additional dowry to the deceased Ramya, the deceased Ramya has committed suicide.
As such, this court has answered the point Nos.1 to 3 in the Negative.
18. Point No.4:
In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 3, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused Nos.1 to 3 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304-B r/w.sec.34 of IPC and Section.3 and 4 of D.P.Act.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of accused persons stand cancelled.
The M.O.1 being door lock and M.O.6 to 10 being clothes of deceased being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after expiry of appeal time.
The M.Os.2 and 3 being gold ornaments are being worthful shall be returned to the deceased parents as per law after expiry of appeal time.

M.Os.4 and 5 being two mobiles are being worthful shall be returned to the deceased parents as per law after expiry of appeal time. (Dictated to the Stenographer, transcript corrected by me and then pronounced in open Court on this the 20th day of December, 2025)
